stories.title: Russell Brand Convicted of Rape and Sexual Assault in London
stories.summary: Russell Brand, a British comedian and actor, was found guilty by a London jury of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The charges stemmed from incidents involving four women between 2005 and 2009. Brand was acquitted of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. He denied the allegations, claiming he never forced anyone against their will.

stories.title: Melania Trump Hosts Russian and Ukrainian Officials to Discuss Ceasefire Progress
stories.summary: Melania Trump hosted delegations from Russia and Ukraine at the White House to discuss a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky. She praised both nations for choosing 'humanity over war' and called for a more enduring truce. The meeting aimed to build on a recent localized ceasefire that allowed for civilian evacuations from the conflict zone.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Retires from International Football at Age 41
stories.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, concluding a career that spanned over two decades with the Portuguese national team. The announcement comes after a recent disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus regarding playing time. Ronaldo's international career included participation in six World Cups and a European Championship title.

stories.title: California Governor Commutes Death Sentences for All Inmates on Death Row
stories.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced the commutation of death sentences for all 548 inmates on death row, converting their sentences to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. This decision reflects his stance against capital punishment, which he deems morally objectionable. Although California has not executed anyone in 20 years, this move does not abolish the death penalty or prevent future prosecutions from seeking it.

stories.title: Paraguay's President Resigns Amid Banking Crisis and Frozen Savings
stories.summary: Santiago Peña, the President of Paraguay, resigned following a severe banking crisis that led to the collapse of Ueno Bank. The central bank intervened, seizing the bank, which had rapidly grown to serve over 60% of the country's adult population. The crisis has raised fears among customers about the safety of their savings.

Experts criticized the trial for potentially denying essential vaccines to thousands of babies, as half of the participants would not receive the vaccine. The trial faced accusations of being unethical and neocolonial.
